d11.why: One sentence puts two things every home-game regular has seen side by side and leaves the viewer to ask why they go together.

d15.why: It opens on the exact sentence the viewer has said out loud and hands it back unfinished.

d03.why: It names the viewer's own table and their own complaint in one breath, with a dry edge that makes the answer feel obvious and still unseen.

d01.why: It contradicts the belief in six words and turns the blame on something the viewer does every session.

d05.why: Anyone who has muttered 'rigged' at an app is caught mid-thought and given something to check instead.

d06.why: It opens inside a moment the viewer has felt, dread at the best hand, before promising a cause other than luck.

d12.why: The player who calls everything is someone the viewer can name, and five of him makes the number a scene.

d20.why: It takes the thing every player blames, the river card, and points at a cause the viewer controls.

d17.why: It denies the bad-luck story in two short sentences and replaces it with a cause the viewer can see at their own table.

d07.why: Feeling safer with suited connectors than with aces is a confession the viewer recognises, and the line says the feeling points at the wrong culprit.
